title: VFD Frequency and Fan Law Calculator
description: A fan selected for 10,000 CFM at 2.00 in. wg and 8.0 bhp on 60 Hz power (illustrative) runs on a VFD. For 45, 30 and 50 Hz the learner predicts airflow, static pressure and brake horsepower (each within 2% of the fan-law model, two attempts); Explore mode then sweeps 20 to 60 Hz with a plot of percent airflow, pressure and power.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Fan performance at reduced VFD frequency
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the airflow, static pressure and brake horsepower of a belt-driven fan at a reduced VFD frequency, using the fan laws with the frequency ratio as the speed ratio, to within 2% of the model values.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, per-value marks and slider readouts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed input borders and solid/dashed feedback borders pair with colour; plot series differ by dash pattern and marker shape; Enter checks and goes on; the slider takes arrow keys.

rules: A prediction is correct when |prediction − model| <= 0.02 × model; all three values are checked together.
Three challenges (45, 30, 50 Hz), fixed order, two attempts each; after the second wrong attempt the model values and worked calculation are shown and the challenge counts as missed.
Display: airflow to 1 CFM, pressure to 0.01 in. wg, power to 0.01 bhp.
assumptions: The system curve passes through zero (no fixed system pressure).
Speed ratio equals frequency ratio; slip and drive losses are ignored.
limitations: Frequencies above 60 Hz are not offered; a speed increase must start with the fan's maximum safe speed in the current catalog.

sources: Base duty: Chapter 15 'Variable Frequency Drive' worked example (illustrative values)
Synchronous speed formula and 1800 RPM at 4 poles, 60 Hz: FanPedia p. 71
Fan laws: standard fan engineering, Chapter 15 and Chapter 25

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict then reveal: a committed three-value prediction per challenge with ratio-based hints, then free exploration of the square and cube curves.
keyQuestions: At 30 Hz, what share of the airflow and what share of the power remain?
Why does a 25% cut in speed cut power by more than half?
commonMisconceptions: Power falls in the same proportion as frequency.
Pressure is unchanged by a speed change.
The VFD changes the motor's number of poles or the sheave ratio.
assessmentOpportunities: Running line 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is all three challenges (nine values) correct within two attempts.
